Folks —

I ran a focused capacity model based on Elaine's traces and our zaya-70b-q4 profile. High-level assumptions first:

- Model/infra assumptions:
  - Model: zaya-70b-quantized (ours: q4_ks); profiling done on H100-80GB and A100-80GB.
  - Avg tokens per request (in+out): 760 tokens (Elaine's number).
  - Typical response length: 420 tokens (so generation is dominant).
  - KV cache hit rate for repeated prefixes: 12% (from traces).
  - Beam/decoding: greedy; no heavy reranking.
  - Batch window: 12 ms (continuous batching)

- Measured perf (single GPU, p50/p95 latency for full generation):
  - H100-80GB (zaya-70b-q4): ~3,200 tokens/sec sustained; p95 generation-only latency for 420-token output ≈ 135 ms (generation), end-to-end with decoding overhead ≈ 160–175 ms.
  - A100-80GB (zaya-70b-q4): ~2,400 tokens/sec sustained; p95 generation-only ≈ 180–220 ms.

- Mapping to RPS and SLOs:
  - For average request (760 tokens): tokens/sec per GPU -> equivalent RPS capacity = tokens/sec / 760.
    - H100: 3200 / 760 ≈ 4.2 RPS per GPU (sustained)
    - A100: 2400 / 760 ≈ 3.2 RPS per GPU
  - To meet p95 <= 350ms at steady state we need generation p95 << 350ms to allow infra and network overhead; H100 meets this comfortably; A100 is borderline at p95 generation-only ~200ms.

- Headroom / burst sizing (target: absorb 230 RPS spikes for 3 minutes):
  - Required RPS capacity for peak with 20% buffer: 230 * 1.2 = 276 RPS
  - GPUs needed (sustained capacity math):
    - H100: 276 / 4.2 ≈ 66 GPUs -> round up to 70 GPUs to ensure distribution and failover (10% extra).
    - A100: 276 / 3.2 ≈ 87 GPUs -> round up to 95 GPUs (include 9% extra + buffer).

- Steady-state baseline (95 RPS typical):
    - H100: 95 / 4.2 ≈ 23 GPUs -> suggest reserving 26 GPUs (≈15% steady buffer).
    - A100: 95 / 3.2 ≈ 30 GPUs -> reserve 34 GPUs.

- Autoscaling / burst strategy recommendation:
  1) Reserve baseline (26 H100) to cover steady-state + short-term buffer; commit for pilot to get price leverage.
  2) Configure burst elastic pool (on-demand) to add up to +44 H100 GPUs for peaks; use fast-warm nodes and model variant fallback to a smaller quantized profile if spin-up delays exceed 30s.
  3) Implement request-level shed/fallback at RB layer: route non-critical search queries to a cheaper 13B model during extreme shortages.

- Cost sketch (approx, list price multiples omitted for clarity):
  - Pilot (3 months), H100 baseline 26 GPUs + average burst usage equivalent to 18 GPUs across spikes -> effective committed v-time ~44 GPU-months -> estimated committed spend band: ~$220k–$270k for 3 months (depends on discount).

- SLO fit notes:
  - H100 baseline + burst with the recommended buffer meets p95 <= 350ms for chat in >98% of windows per trace simulation.
  - If Quantus insists on p99 <= 350ms, we'd need additional reserve (add 15–20% more GPUs) or more aggressive KV caching (improve hit rate) and prompt prefix normalization.

Next steps I recommend:
- Rafael: confirm which GPU family Quantus prefers (H100 vs A100) and whether they can accept p99 <= 1s for search (eases sizing).
- Marissa: confirm discount band / committed spend threshold for the pilot so I can adjust the cost sketch.
- Elaine: confirm Q4 plan for 32k context — that increases memory pressure and may change per-GPU tokens/sec by -8% (needs re-profile).

I uploaded the detailed workbook (quantus_capacity_model_v2.xlsx) with per-minute RPS projections, per-GPU load curves, and sensitivity runs for KV hit rate (8%/12%/20%).

- Dev
Senior Inference Engineer
Redwood Inference
